change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request, and its full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement. The reason given is that the indoor temperature records analysed in the paper were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the withdrawal statement says the reported results cannot be relied on. The stored paper reported that the mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats was 2.1 °C lower than in the paired control flats, and that living rooms in green-roofed flats spent 41% fewer hours above 28 °C. Those results came from indoor air temperature logged every ten minutes in the flats. The paper's indoor-temperature findings, including the 2.1 °C and 41% results, can no longer be relied on.
evaluation: In Section 2.2 (Methods), the draft sets the indoor cooling effect of a green roof in its model to 2.1 °C, the reduction measured in the paired field study by Okafor et al. [14], and the stored paper reported that the mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats was 2.1 °C lower than in the paired control flats. The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request: the withdrawal statement says its indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and it says the reported results cannot be relied on. The Methods use of the 2.1 °C value is touched by the withdrawal, and the draft's Results estimate that green roofs avoid about half of person-hours uses the green-roof parameter from Section 2.2. In the Discussion, the draft says its green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C reduction taken from Okafor et al. [14], and that if the value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings, so the Discussion use is touched too. The impact on the draft is high.
recommendation: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request: the withdrawal statement says the paper's indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and it says the reported results cannot be relied on. In Section 2.2 (Methods), the draft sets the indoor cooling effect of a green roof in its model to 2.1 °C, the reduction measured in the paired field study by Okafor et al. [14], and the draft's Results estimate that green roofs avoid about half of person-hours uses the green-roof parameter from Section 2.2, while in the Discussion, the draft says its green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C reduction taken from Okafor et al. [14]. Before you edit any text, raise this with your co-authors or supervisor. You will need a green-roof parameter from a reliable source in place of the 2.1 °C value, and the model will need to be rerun. Then remove the citation to [14] as the source of the 2.1 °C value, and re-check the Results estimate and the Discussion's comparison with reflective coatings against the new output.

explanation.text: In Section 2.2 (Methods), the draft sets the indoor cooling effect of a green roof in its model to 2.1 °C, the reduction measured in the paired field study by Okafor et al. [14], and the stored paper reported that the mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats was 2.1 °C lower than in the paired control flats.

The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request: the withdrawal statement says its indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and it says the reported results cannot be relied on.
The Methods use of the 2.1 °C value is touched by the withdrawal, and the draft's Results estimate that green roofs avoid about half of person-hours uses the green-roof parameter from Section 2.2.

In the Discussion, the draft says its green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C reduction taken from Okafor et al. [14], and that if the value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings, so the Discussion use is touched too.
The impact on the draft is high.
